scope: code routing table (W_code) for the bridge/door layer: truck123d/src/bd_bridge.rs, binding.rs, marshal.rs, facade.rs, lib.rs; corpus/ttc/door.py engine/op dispatch; cross-referenced to docs/OP_CAPABILITY_MATRIX.md cells

rules.discriminator: argv[0] == "--engine" -> ENGINE = argv[1] (occ default, truck the kernel regime)
rules.theorem_comment: ``--engine`` selects the regime: ``occ`` (default, the OCC baseline) or ``truck`` (the kernel-engine regime landed by TTC-EXECUTOR-BINDING ...).

rules.discriminator: ENGINE == "truck" -> install_truck_alias(); else install_cadgen_alias()
rules.theorem_comment: The kernel-engine regime: the alias installs the truck drop-in module (bd_bridge over truck123d) instead of build123d.

rules.discriminator: installs the build123d-named data-recording surface; all geometry deferred to truck123d.bd_facts/bd_stl
rules.theorem_comment: A name whose carrier form the executor does not cover raises the mapped ``truck123d.Refused`` exception -- loud, never a silent fallback to OCC.

rules.discriminator: ENGINE != truck -> genuine build123d (OCC) is the dispatch target
rules.theorem_comment: Answer the corpus imports ``cadgen.build123d`` ... with the genuine build123d package.

rules.discriminator: every drop-in arm whose carrier form the executor cannot answer calls _refuse(message)
rules.theorem_comment: Raise the mapped truck exception for a name the executor cannot answer (typed, never a bare Exception or a silent fallback).

rules.discriminator: _TRUCK_NAMES census vocabulary answered name-for-name; Shape/Solid mixins add cast/make_cylinder/make_sphere

outcomes.variant: bd module with every census name

rules.theorem_comment: Every name is answered (signatures never improved); names whose carrier form the landed executor cannot answer refuse with the mapped typed exception.

rules.discriminator: operator/mode union|subtract|intersect over two _Shape operands; a _BooleanResult operand refuses BooleanResultOperand (depth-1 only)
refusals: _refuse("a boolean operand outside a kernel-engine row ...")
_refuse("BooleanResultOperand: a boolean of a boolean result ...")
rules.theorem_comment: The operands' LOCAL geometry is what dispatches; a placed operand's frame composes after (the recorded exactness rule), so admission is placement-blind and verdict-stable.

rules.discriminator: Face profile + full 360 arc -> lathe row (z-axis legacy or non-z axis profile+frame); partial arc / non-Face / degenerate axis / open profile / spline-with-options refuse
refusals: _refuse("a partial-arc revolve is outside the executor's lathe arm")
_refuse("a revolve profile outside the y=0 plane ...")
_refuse("a spline-profile revolve is not a kernel-engine row")
_refuse("an axis parallel to its profile ray ...")
rules.theorem_comment: A partial arc, a degenerate axis, a profile that is not a single-sided meridian generator about the axis, an open profile, or a spline whose interpolation options the recorded data cannot recover refuses typed.

rules.discriminator: Face boundary all-line -> prism row; boundary carrying a recorded spline -> trim_prism row dispatched through bd_facts at record time
refusals: _refuse("Face extrusion is not yet a kernel-engine row")
trim_prism constructor typed refusal surfaced at record time
rules.theorem_comment: A boundary carrying a recorded spline edge is the spline-trimmed extrude constructor row (`trim_prism`) ... The row is dispatched through the native facts entry at record time.

rules.discriminator: line path -> 2-station loft chain; spline path -> chain over recorded samples; section outside line-loop vocabulary refuses
refusals: _refuse("a path outside the recorded line/spline edge carrier ...")
_refuse("a section outside the recorded Face carrier ...")
rules.theorem_comment: Each station places the section through the fixed-order double-reflection frames (parallel transport, never Frenet).

rules.discriminator: ordered Face section list -> Loft row; non-Face section or empty list -> _LOFT_REFUSAL
refusals: _refuse at facts arm for a spline-section smooth volume
rules.theorem_comment: The kernel certifies the ruled matched-vertex chain with exact facts for all-line sections; a spline-section loft's smooth-surface volume is an open carrier the executor refuses typed at the facts arm.

rules.discriminator: about is a coordinate Plane (XY->z, XZ->y, YZ->x); any other carrier or a second different plane refuses
rules.theorem_comment: A mirror about a coordinate plane records a placed-carrier transform over the mirrored census row (the landed placed/processor rule): the solid carrier is untouched and the facts transform with the placement -- no geometry is recomputed.

rules.discriminator: any fillet call -> immediate typed refusal (no edge topology on the drop-in)
rules.theorem_comment: An empty entity selection: the drop-in records no fillet/chamfer edge topology, so ``shape.edges()``/``shape.faces()`` yield nothing and the corpus's ``safe_fillet``/``safe_chamfer`` ladders return the shape.

rules.discriminator: any chamfer call -> immediate typed refusal
rules.theorem_comment: See door.fillet: the drop-in records no edge topology for a blend arm.

rules.discriminator: any Circle(radius) -> immediate typed refusal (a circle is an exact conic, not a recoverable line/spline carrier)
refusals: _refuse("a circle profile is not answered exactly by a kernel-engine row")
rules.theorem_comment: A circle is an exact conic, not a recoverable line/spline carrier: feeding it to ``loft``/``extrude``/``revolve`` cannot be answered exactly by the landed executor, so the carrier keeps its typed refusal.

rules.discriminator: Box(length,width,height) -> SolidSpec::Box
rules.theorem_comment: build123d ``Box(length, width, height)`` (centered on the origin).

rules.discriminator: rotation (0,0,0)->z, (90,0,0)->y, (0,90,0)->x; z-rotated or other rotations refuse
refusals: _refuse("z-rotated cylinders are not a kernel-engine row")
_refuse("this cylinder rotation is not a census carrier")
rules.theorem_comment: build123d ``Cylinder(radius, height)`` (centered, z-axis by default).

rules.discriminator: Sphere(radius) -> SolidSpec::Sphere
rules.theorem_comment: build123d ``Sphere(radius)`` (centered on the origin).

rules.discriminator: major_angle == 360 -> SolidSpec::Torus; partial-arc torus refuses
refusals: _refuse("a partial-arc torus is not a kernel-engine row")
rules.theorem_comment: build123d ``Torus(major_radius, minor_radius)`` (centered, z-axis).

source.symbol: door.Edge.make_line / Edge.make_spline / door.Spline / door.Line / door.Polyline / door.Polygon / door.make_face

rules.discriminator: recorded defining samples only (line endpoints or spline sample list); never a flattening polygon
refusals: _refuse("a polygon profile needs at least three points")
_refuse("make_face is not a corpus kernel-engine carrier")
_refuse("this path carrier has no recorded interpolation")
rules.theorem_comment: The edge records its DEFINING samples (the points the corpus passed) as a data row; a consuming verb answers exactly where the executor can ... and refuses typed where the exact carrier is genuinely open.

source.symbol: door.Vector / door.Plane / door.Pos / door.Location / door.Rotation / door.Rot / door._Frame

rules.discriminator: Vector is pure client-side direction data; Plane/Pos/Location/Rotation record an orthonormal frame; frame*shape records the placement
refusals: _refuse("Plane forms beyond a frame row are not census carriers")
_refuse("Location forms beyond a frame row are not census carriers")
rules.theorem_comment: ``Plane(origin, x_dir, z_dir)`` and the ``Plane.XY/XZ/YZ`` markers record an orthonormal frame ... placing algebra (``frame * shape``) records the placement.

rules.discriminator: children/obj list -> group node; _leaves() flattens for solids()
rules.theorem_comment: build123d ``Compound``: a group of child construction rows.

rules.discriminator: list of (prototype, location, name) -> placed.moved(location) then Compound
rules.theorem_comment: ``compound_from_instances`` (a cadgen composition helper the Falcon-Heavy tree uses to place repeated engine instances) is answered with the equivalent plain build123d composition.

rules.discriminator: obj.solids()/obj.volume/obj.bounding_box() -> _T123D.bd_facts(node JSON)
refusals: facts["err:<type>"] recorded per-field on any exception (door reports, never crashes)
rules.theorem_comment: All geometry lives behind the native executor; this side only records data and frames.

rules.discriminator: ENGINE==truck -> _T123D.bd_stl(node); else bd.export_stl(tolerance=diag*2e-4, angular_tolerance=0.5)
refusals: door main catches a refused export as a typed verdict (record.ok=false)
rules.theorem_comment: The kernel executor writes the deterministic triangle soup of the submitted construction tree.

rules.discriminator: Shape.cast(wrapped) -> typed refusal (no OCC wrapping)
rules.theorem_comment: A corpus helper that probes the wrapped OCC shape of a kernel-engine data row cannot be served: refuse typed rather than pass `None` into OCP.

rules.discriminator: any access to .wrapped on a truck row -> typed refusal
refusals: _refuse("an OCC probe of a kernel-engine row is not a kernel-engine row")
rules.theorem_comment: An OCC probe of a kernel-engine data row cannot be served: refuse typed rather than pass `None` into OCP (which would die as an untyped TypeError).

rules.discriminator: build then facts then export; any exception is reported as a typed ttc_door_run.v1 record (ok=false)

outcomes.variant: record ok=true with facts and triangle count
record ok=false with error.kind and payload

refusals: typed exception marshaled into the record (never an untyped crash)
rules.theorem_comment: The door reports typed failure ... wall time is recorded but never asserted.

rules.discriminator: pyo3 entry: parse FacadeTable JSON -> run_facade; a refusal is marshaled to Refused/Unresolved
rules.theorem_comment: The pyo3 wrapper over [`run_facade`]: parses the submitted table JSON, runs the facade, and returns the report JSON.

rules.discriminator: ordered FacadeOp match: Sweep|Loft, Spline, Polygon|Polyline|Circle, primitives+Extrude|Revolve|RevolveArc, MakeFace, Mirror, Mode, selectors, Fillet|Chamfer, ExportStl, ExportStep, PushPart, PushSketch, Pop
refusals: Refusal::Empty (empty export domain / blend with no selection)
rules.theorem_comment: Every entry point lands here as one Rust fn taking the submitted table -- [`run_facade`] -- so the native Rust facade entry calls the same fn without Python.

rules.discriminator: pending_mode None -> advance carrier; Some(mode) -> dispatch_swept_carrier_boolean(base, produced, mode)
rules.theorem_comment: Resolves the pending `Mode` row (the swept-carrier boolean dispatch) and records routed rows or refuses typed, then advances the current carrier.

rules.discriminator: carrier-class pair + mode; canonical x canonical -> CanonicalLanded; torus -> ContactReductionDeferred; not admitted -> NonCanonicalCarrier; else Routed
rules.theorem_comment: This is the deterministic per-pair mirror of the kernel's CL-006 `dispatch_restricted_sweep`; the loop-side facade cannot name the certified crate ... so the certified outcome is asserted here at the pair-verdict granularity the report layer consumes.

rules.discriminator: admit unless (base == Swept && tool == Swept)
rules.theorem_comment: A pair coupling TWO lofted/swept carriers (the `Swept` x `Swept` cell) is the pair cell the certified funnel does NOT admit end to end at this coarse granularity (the PB-011C census).

rules.discriminator: base == Torus || tool == Torus -> ContactReductionDeferred
rules.theorem_comment: a pair coupling a swept carrier with a torus carrier is a class the funnel refuses (the torus is excluded from the implicit-reduction stage, Theorem 4 economics) and answers the typed, localized `ContactReductionDeferred` refusal.

rules.discriminator: constructive == true -> NonCanonicalCarrier; solid_ops == 0 -> Empty; else record export_step
rules.theorem_comment: TR-NRB-001: STEP out of constructive/swept surfaces is a typed kernel refusal, never a silent STL fallback.

rules.discriminator: selection_pending == false -> Refusal::Empty
rules.theorem_comment: A blend row must bind the selection rows recorded immediately before it in the same frame; a blend with no recorded selection is an empty edge domain and refuses (`Refusal::Empty`).

rules.discriminator: op -> carrier class; Extrude/Revolve/RevolveArc key on the profile carrier (Spline -> Swept/Revolved)
rules.theorem_comment: The carrier class a solid-producing op yields, or `None` for an op that does not change the current solid's carrier.

rules.discriminator: base is a funnel carrier -> base, else tool
rules.theorem_comment: The product carrier class of a boolean: a swept product stays in the swept family (the base class when the base is a swept carrier, else the tool's).

rules.discriminator: Spline op -> constructive=true, profile=Spline
rules.theorem_comment: A spline carrier is a non-canonical carrier: any part built over one is constructive for the STEP boundary.

rules.discriminator: Polygon/Polyline/Circle -> profile=Canonical (not constructive by themselves)
rules.theorem_comment: A circle is an exact conic profile, canonical like a polygon; only the constructive verbs over one mark the part constructive.

rules.discriminator: Mode{value} -> pending_mode = Some(value); armed until the next solid op
rules.theorem_comment: The `Mode` row is the facade's `boolean_op` encoding: it arms the boolean that the next solid op performs.

rules.discriminator: Mirror{axis} -> solid_ops+=1, carrier unchanged (a mirrored swept product is still swept)
rules.theorem_comment: A mirror keeps the part's carrier class (and its STEP constructiveness): a mirrored swept product is still swept.

rules.discriminator: PushPart resets carrier+profile+pending_mode; PushSketch resets profile; Pop is a no-op on the carrier
rules.theorem_comment: A fresh part frame starts canonical; a part opened inside another frame inherits nothing from the enclosing part.

rules.discriminator: pyo3 entry: parse_tree -> tree_facts under GIL release; serialize {solid_count,volume,bbox[,seam_mismatch][,boolean_events]}
refusals: typed kernel refusal marshaled by refusal_to_pyerr
rules.theorem_comment: The pyo3 measurement entry: takes the construction tree JSON and returns the facts JSON (`{solid_count, volume, bbox}`).

rules.discriminator: pyo3 entry: parse_tree -> write_tree_stl under GIL release; returns {triangles:n}
refusals: Refusal::Empty (parse failure or empty triangle soup)
typed kernel refusal marshaled by refusal_to_pyerr
rules.theorem_comment: The pyo3 export entry: writes the construction tree's STL to `path` and returns `{"triangles": n}`.

rules.discriminator: serde_json from_str into TreeNode (untagged Part|Group|Boolean); any parse error -> Refusal::Empty
rules.theorem_comment: Parses a submitted construction tree JSON.

rules.discriminator: count_and_union then top_volume then top_seam_mismatch then collect_boolean_events; empty tree -> Empty
rules.theorem_comment: Measures the submitted tree with the recorded OCC top-node semantics.

rules.discriminator: Part -> count++ + union part_world_bbox; Boolean -> dispatch_boolean then recurse base a; Group -> recurse children
rules.theorem_comment: Recursively counts every part and unions every part's world bbox.

rules.discriminator: Part -> solid_volume; Boolean -> dispatch_boolean then volume of base a; Group -> sum immediate child Parts/Booleans only (nested groups contribute nothing)
rules.theorem_comment: A group sums only its immediate child parts (nested groups contribute nothing, mirroring the OCC `Compound` measurement the reference was recorded with).

rules.discriminator: single Part with Loft{closed:true} -> loft_seam_mismatch; closed smooth -> open_smooth_loft; Boolean -> dispatch then base a; Group -> None
rules.theorem_comment: The seam certificate of a single closed halo loft row ... the aligned meeting edges across the chain closure satisfy `A0 W1 - A1 W0 == 0`.

rules.discriminator: Part -> noop; Group -> recurse; Boolean -> dispatch_boolean, push event if Some
rules.theorem_comment: Collects the routed boolean events of a tree, in script order, and validates every row.

rules.discriminator: node_carrier_class(a), node_carrier_class(b) -> facade::dispatch_swept_carrier_boolean(base, tool, mode); CanonicalLanded -> None; Routed -> Some(event); Refused -> Err
rules.theorem_comment: Dispatches one recorded boolean row through the facade's boolean entry ... and returns the routed event. The dispatch is placement-blind: it sees each operand's LOCAL carrier class.

rules.discriminator: Part -> solid_carrier_class(local solid); Group -> first part in order; Boolean -> Refusal::UnsupportedEnvelope(NonCanonicalCarrier) (depth-2)
rules.theorem_comment: A placed part classifies by its LOCAL solid (the dispatch never sees a placement); a boolean operand is the recorded depth-2 open composition cell and refuses typed.

rules.discriminator: Box|Cylinder|Sphere|Prism -> Canonical; TrimPrism -> Swept if spline idiom else Canonical; Torus -> Torus; Lathe -> Revolved if any spline edge else Canonical; Loft|Member -> Swept
rules.theorem_comment: The corpus spline-profile extrude carries a spline side surface, so it classifies as the `Swept` carrier the facade's `Extrude` over a spline profile produces; a line-base trim row keeps the canonical class.

rules.discriminator: SolidSpec tag -> closed-form volume
rules.theorem_comment: The analytic volume of one unplaced solid.

rules.discriminator: arc_deg != 360 -> NonCanonicalCarrier; all-line profile -> lathe_volume (frustum telescoping); spline profile -> lathe_profile_volume (true reconstructed interpolant)
rules.theorem_comment: The partial-arc form is a certified facade op (PB-014), but this executor's analytic lathe arm covers the full revolution; a partial arc refuses typed, never approximates.

rules.discriminator: prism_geom over the closed planar line-loop profile; spline edge -> NonCanonicalCarrier via profile_loop
rules.theorem_comment: The extruded solid is an exact prism: the volume is the profile area times the swept length (`amount`, or `2 * amount` when `both`).

rules.discriminator: is_spline_profile_prism -> spline_profile_prism_facts (exact reconstructed spline loop prism); else binding::trim_extrude_solid (algebraic trim constructor)

preconditions.value: !unmodeled:empty base + closed spline curve, or line base + trim

rules.theorem_comment: The composition itself lives in the binding layer (`crate::python::binding::trim_extrude`); this arm is a pure pass-through so the door vocabulary reaches the constructor.

rules.discriminator: loft_sections Ok -> loft_volume (exact ruled, bit-identical V5); else closed -> open_smooth_loft; else certified_spline_loft_volume (smooth certified bracket)
rules.theorem_comment: The landed analytic ruled arm stays the fast path for the class it already certifies (V5: bit-identical). A spline-section carrier falls to the certified smooth arm; a closed halo chain has no smooth certificate.

rules.discriminator: member_volume_bracket(profile, stations, ruled): all-line plate -> exact loft_volume; else sum MONO-2 two-station certificates; smooth >2 stations -> open_smooth_loft
rules.theorem_comment: A member is a two-section degenerate case plus wall bands, so its certified facts ride the landed MONO-2 two-station loft certificate per adjacent station pair rather than a new integrator.

rules.discriminator: per SolidSpec tag; Lathe line vs spline; TrimPrism spline idiom vs constructor; Loft ruled vs smooth (+ control-net enclosure for N>2); Member via spline_loop_bbox3
rules.theorem_comment: The exact AABB of a profile loop: the support of any axis-aligned linear function over a polygon is attained at a polygon vertex, so the loop's bbox over its vertices is exact for the loop region.

rules.discriminator: local bbox -> mirror_point if part.mirror -> RotationFrame.apply (or rz rotation) -> translate (x,y,z); AABB of 8 corners
rules.theorem_comment: The AABB of the 8 rotated local corners is the exact world bbox under the orthonormal placement rotation.

rules.discriminator: per SolidSpec tag; Part applies mirror then rotation/rz then translation; Boolean -> base a; Group -> children
rules.theorem_comment: The mirror placed-carrier reflects the local geometry before the rz rotation and translation (no geometry recomputation).

rules.discriminator: line edges exactly; spline edges sampled at fixed SPLINE_MESH_STEPS per reconstructed span; ring swept over MESH_SEGMENTS
rules.theorem_comment: For an all-line profile the ring is exactly the vertex loop, so the mesh is identical to the landed line-profile mesh.

rules.discriminator: prism_geom -> side quads between bottom/top rings plus cap fans
rules.theorem_comment: The local mesh of an extruded prism: the profile boundary swept between the two end planes plus cap fans. Deterministic, closed, no duplicate vertices.

rules.discriminator: loft_sections Ok -> ruled quads + end caps; else closed -> open_smooth_loft; else spline_loft_mesh
rules.theorem_comment: The certified spline-section class meshes through the reconstructed ruled surface; a closed smooth chain has no certificate.

rules.discriminator: member_sections -> spline_loop_spans/sample_loop3 per station -> ruled quads + end-cap fans
rules.theorem_comment: The sampled loops are the same reconstruction the certificate integrates.

rules.discriminator: spline_loop_spans per section; equal span counts; station_params; per-span Bernstein grids -> binding::volume_facts (certify_patch_form); plus exact end-cap moments
refusals: open_smooth_loft (span count 0 / unequal loops / zero area)
rules.theorem_comment: The section ... is assembled over the sanctioned `binding_volume_facts` entry, summing the certified brackets ... plus the exact planar end-cap moments.

rules.discriminator: member_sections -> loft_sections Ok => exact loft_volume; !ruled && >2 => open_smooth_loft; else sum certified_spline_loft_volume over adjacent pairs
rules.theorem_comment: The interior caps of consecutive pairs cancel exactly, so the sum is the chain's side surface plus its two end caps -- 'a two-section degenerate case plus wall bands'.

rules.discriminator: mirror axis "x"|"z"|else "y" applied to local points/triangles and local bbox before placement
rules.theorem_comment: The mirror placed-carrier reflects the local geometry before the rz rotation and translation (no geometry recomputation).

rules.discriminator: tree_mesh -> binary STL (80-byte header, u32 count, per-tri zero normal + 3 f32 vertices + u16 attr)
refusals: Refusal::Empty (empty triangle soup / count overflow / write failure)
rules.theorem_comment: Writes the tree's triangle soup as a binary STL file at `path`, returning the triangle count.

rules.discriminator: serde internally-tagged enum on "kind": box|cylinder|sphere|torus|lathe|prism|trim_prism|loft|member; deny_unknown_fields
rules.theorem_comment: The solid carrier of one construction row. Data only: every field is a physical length/angle the corpus script computed.

rules.discriminator: registers the restricted-pair solver and the SSI-admit solver into the truck-evidence trait-object registries
rules.theorem_comment: The concrete 'call the impls through the trait objects' step: the certified impls land in the registry slots the funnel dispatches through.

rules.discriminator: register_certified_entries -> facade mirror verdict; Routed -> certify_transverse_pair over recorded cones; CanonicalLanded/Refused -> typed outcome
refusals: EnvelopeCase::ContactReductionDeferred / NonCanonicalCarrier via the facade mirror
rules.theorem_comment: A routed pair actually runs the certified Theorem C transversality certificate over the row's recorded certified normal cones and returns the certified `‖n_X × n_Y‖` bracket.

rules.discriminator: TensorBernsteinPatch::try_new over the recorded grids -> certify_patch_form with orientation; bracket out
rules.theorem_comment: The certified volume-facts entry: assemble the recorded patch row and run the landed certified face-form volume fact, returning its two-sided bracket.

rules.discriminator: certify_algebraic_trim_bracket(density, trim, tolerance) -> two-sided integral bracket
rules.theorem_comment: The certified trim-facts entry for the algebraic-trim path: run the landed certified algebraic-trim bracket engine over the recorded pullback nets.

rules.discriminator: fit_plane -> line_loop_vertices or bbox_rect; no trim -> prism_geom; self-crossing -> TrimClipFailed; no net -> trim_pullback_missing; degree > 16 -> trim_degree_out_of_envelope; else build_graph + bezier_trim_leaf + trim_clip + certify_algebraic_trim_bracket
rules.theorem_comment: A trim class the composition cannot close (a self-crossing control loop, a trim with no recorded pullback net, a stalled R9 isolation) refuses TYPED naming the `TrimClipFailed` family -- Inconclusive, never silent (§9.4).

rules.discriminator: trim_extrude(row) then prism_mesh over the reconstructed base profile
rules.theorem_comment: The realized facts of one trim-prism row: the certified volume value plus the deterministic local mesh of the base extrusion.

rules.discriminator: ShapeRow -> patch_rigorous_bbox (Bernstein hull subdivision to DATA_ROW_BBOX_SLACK)
rules.theorem_comment: Every boundary patch is a rational tensor-Bernstein patch `X = Â/Ŵ` with certified positive weights, so its affine control net `Â_ij / Ŵ_ij` bounds the patch by the convex-hull property.

rules.discriminator: ShapeRow -> bbox bound carried into the recorded frame (lo,hi corner-pair form)
rules.theorem_comment: `obox` is the same bound carried into the row's recorded frame (the `lo, hi` corner-pair form the corpus helper consumes).

rules.discriminator: ShapeRow closed && oriented -> the recorded 2-cycle invariant (never an OCC probe)
rules.theorem_comment: `is_valid_shape` -- the landed closed/oriented 2-cycle invariant the row recorded at construction. Never an OCC probe.

rules.discriminator: ShapeRow -> number of patches of the boundary grid
rules.theorem_comment: `face_count` -- the number of patches of the row's boundary grid.

rules.discriminator: module registers only marshal_refused, marshal_unresolved, kernel_evidence_compose, facade_submit, bd_facts, bd_stl; the binding.rs #[pyfunction]s are NOT registered
rules.theorem_comment: The drop-in executor binding (TTC-EXECUTOR-BINDING): the two geometry entries the corpus-door kernel-engine regime drives.

rules.discriminator: exhaustive match on the base Refusal variant -> Refused|Unresolved typed payload

outcomes.variant: ExceptionClass::Refused (Empty, UnsupportedEnvelope, CompositionMarginExhausted, InputOutsideBackwardBudget, Contradictory, Collapsed, ForwardToleranceExceeded)

rules.theorem_comment: The match is exhaustive: adding a `Refusal` variant later breaks this function on purpose.

rules.discriminator: EnvelopeCase -> snake_case name (6 variants)
rules.theorem_comment: `EnvelopeCase` -> snake_case name. Exhaustive; the six payloads of §2.

rules.discriminator: ConstructRefusal -> single booked door case construct_refused, variant tag on payload.stage
rules.theorem_comment: Every construct-stage refusal maps onto the single booked `construct_refused` door case (the detailed variant rides the payload).

rules.discriminator: UnmappedRefusal -> Refused{case:unmapped_refusal, stage:kind}

preconditions.value: !unmodeled:certified RefusalKind with no booked door mapping

rules.theorem_comment: Marshals an unmapped certified refusal kind as the typed [`UnmappedRefusal`] defect signal: `Refused` class, `unmapped_refusal` case ... never a bare string, never a silent approximation.

rules.discriminator: RefusalKind -> snake_case name (25 variants)
rules.theorem_comment: Exhaustive over the frozen 25-variant set; a new variant breaks this function on purpose (the mapping table must be extended by spec edit, not by a silent wildcard).

rules.discriminator: RefusalKind -> name -> DoorCase
rules.theorem_comment: Total over the frozen 25-variant set; the name table is the single mapping source.

rules.discriminator: name -> DoorCase; construct/carrier -> ConstructRefused; envelope -> UnsupportedEnvelope; contradictory -> Contradictory; collapse -> Collapsed; non_finite -> ForwardToleranceExceeded; inconclusive -> NumericallyUnresolved; else UnmappedRefusal
rules.theorem_comment: Every §17 variant is booked here; a name the table does not hold is the typed [`DoorCase::UnmappedRefusal`] defect signal -- never silent, never a guess.

rules.discriminator: Refusal -> Marshaled::from_refusal -> marshal_refused|marshal_unresolved
refusals: typed exception only; never a bare Exception
rules.theorem_comment: Maps a typed kernel refusal to the mapped Python exception (the landed `Refused`/`Unresolved` classes), never a bare `Exception`.

rules.discriminator: BindingError::Malformed -> Refusal::Empty; BindingError::Refusal(_) -> Refusal::UnsupportedEnvelope(NonCanonicalCarrier)
rules.theorem_comment: The executor's `Refusal` vocabulary carries the typed envelope case the door already re-marshals, so no refusal is ever lost or turned into a panic.

rules.discriminator: run_facade Err(refusal) -> Marshaled::from_refusal -> marshal_refused|marshal_unresolved
rules.theorem_comment: A typed kernel refusal ... raises the `Refused`/`Unresolved` exception with the marshaled payload -- never a bare `Exception`.

unmodeled_values: !unmodeled:profile empty base + closed spline curve, or line base + trim
!unmodeled:refusal certified RefusalKind with no booked door mapping

matrix_cells.refinement: both-Swept refuses at the facade admission consult (D-FACADE-ADMISSION-CONSULT) and the refusal propagates through D-BRIDGE-DISPATCH-BOOLEAN as Refusal::UnsupportedEnvelope(NonCanonicalCarrier); the door's _boolean row surfaces it at record time. The coarse cell 'refuses' is one semantic route, not one corpus model.

Cell 'refuses' vs code 'facade-mirror Routed, no certified dispatch' is a ROUTING GAP.

routing_gaps.title: certified swept-carrier boolean dispatch is unreachable from the bridge/door path
routing_gaps.detail: bd_bridge::dispatch_boolean (bd_bridge.rs:2869) consults only facade::dispatch_swept_carrier_boolean (the pure-Rust admission mirror). When that returns BooleanPairVerdict::Routed, bd_bridge records a SweptBooleanEvent and then measures the BASE operand (top_volume/count_and_union/append_node_mesh recurse boolean.a). It never calls crate::python::binding::boolean_dispatch (binding.rs:286), which is the only route to construct::admission::certify_transverse_pair (fragment B rule ADMISSION-CERTIFY-TRANSVERSE-PAIR). W_theory contains the Theorem C transversality rule; W_code never reaches it. The coarse matrix cells 2-6 read 'refuses' but the semantic route is 'facade-mirror Routed, product never computed'.

routing_gaps.title: binding.rs pyo3 exports are not registered in the module
routing_gaps.detail: lib.rs::truck123d (lib.rs:62) registers only marshal_refused, marshal_unresolved, kernel_evidence_compose, facade_submit, bd_facts, bd_stl. The eight binding.rs #[pyfunction]s (binding_boolean_dispatch, binding_volume_facts, binding_trim_facts, binding_trim_extrude, binding_bbox, binding_obox, binding_is_valid_shape, binding_face_count) are never added, so Python cannot call them. door.py calls only _T123D.bd_facts, _T123D.bd_stl and _T123D.Refused. The certified boolean entry the door shim was supposed to flip against is unreachable.

routing_gaps.title: certified solver registry is never populated on the door path
routing_gaps.detail: register_certified_entries (binding.rs:276) is called only from binding::boolean_dispatch, which RG-1 shows is unreachable. Therefore construct::bie::ssi4::register_restricted_pair_solver and ssi_admit::register_ssi_admit_solver never run for a door submission; the truck-evidence trait-object registry slots the funnel dispatches through stay empty.

routing_gaps.title: boolean product is never computed; only the base operand is measured
routing_gaps.detail: For every boolean node (canonical x canonical included), top_volume/count_and_union/append_node_mesh recurse the base operand a and ignore b. Canonical x canonical reports CanonicalLanded and measures a; swept pairs record an event and measure a. No subtraction/union/intersection of the two solids is realized in the executor, so the door's volume/bbox/STL describe the base operand, not the boolean result.

routing_gaps.title: partial-arc revolve matrix cell unreachable through the door
routing_gaps.detail: OP_CAPABILITY_MATRIX cell 10 (revolve(partial-arc,spline-profile)) is marked certified (flipped by PB-014). The door drop-in refuses revolution_arc != 360 (door.py:1380) and bd_bridge's Lathe volume/bbox/mesh arms refuse arc_deg != 360 with NonCanonicalCarrier (bd_bridge.rs:436). The landed PB-014 route is the facade RevolveArc row (facade.rs:417), which only runs through facade_submit -- a surface door.py never calls. The coarse cell and the door code disagree.

routing_gaps.title: circle/fillet/chamfer matrix cells certified but refused by the door drop-in
routing_gaps.detail: Cells 14 (fillet), 15 (chamfer) and 19 (author(circle-profile)) are marked certified, and the facade table has Fillet/Chamfer/Circle rows. The door drop-in refuses all three unconditionally (door.py:2046, 2050, 807) because it records no edge topology and no conic profile. The facade rows are only reachable through facade_submit, which door.py never calls.

routing_gaps.title: facade table path and bridge path are disjoint; door measures only the bridge
routing_gaps.detail: door.py routes through install_truck_alias -> bd_facts/bd_stl (bd_bridge.rs). It never calls facade_submit/run_facade. So all facade.rs swept-carrier routing (PB-011 G1), the ExportStep TR-NRB-001 refusal, and the Fillet/Chamfer/Circle/RevolveArc rows are dead relative to the door: 'the lift ran green through the FACADE path but the timing measured the DOOR path'.

routing_gaps.title: engine regime divergence: occ path serves what truck refuses
routing_gaps.detail: door.py --engine occ installs genuine build123d (install_cadgen_alias) and bd.export_stl, so Circle, fillet, chamfer, partial-arc revolve/torus and booleans all run on OCC. The same corpus entry under --engine truck hits the typed refusals above. A green truck lift therefore certifies only the routes the drop-in answers; an occ measurement of the same entry is a different dispatch graph.

routing_gaps.title: reflect_solid is test-only; production mirror is placed-carrier only
routing_gaps.detail: reflect_solid (bd_bridge.rs:2667) carries #[cfg(test)], so no production route reflects a SolidSpec through the volume/bbox/mesh arms. The production mirror is the placed-carrier PartSpec.mirror consumed by part_world_bbox/append_node_mesh/mirror_point. Any theory rule about reflecting the solid's carrier is reached only by the test suite, not by a door submission.

notes: SCOPE: SOLVER-SURVEY-D is the W_code routing survey for the bridge/door layer. Files read: truck123d/src/bd_bridge.rs (6191 lines, anchors A1=185 fn [a-z_] and A2=7 fn member_[a-z_]( verified), binding.rs, marshal.rs, facade.rs, lib.rs, python.rs; corpus/ttc/door.py; docs/OP_CAPABILITY_MATRIX.md (cross-referenced, not re-derived). The rules are routing rows, not math rows: each row records the discriminator that selects the arm, the bridge entry it calls, and the kernel rule ids it REACHES via fragments A-C. Resolved reaches reference fragment rule ids (C-SPLIT-TRIM-CLIP, C-GATE-BEZIERLEAF1-TRY-NEW, C-GATE-POINTCERT-TRY-NEW, C-GATE-ARCCERT-TRY-NEW, C-GATE-FRAME-TRY-NEW, C-SPLIT-CERTIFY-CROSSINGS, C-SPLIT-CERTIFY-OFF-LOOP, C-CLASSIFY-WINDING-NUMBER, C-CLASSIFY-SAMPLE-INSIDE, ADMISSION-CERTIFY-TRANSVERSE-PAIR) and D-scope rule ids; unresolved kernel symbols stay exact paths (construct::volume_facts::certify_patch_form, construct::volume_facts::certify_algebraic_trim_bracket, construct::bie::ssi4::register_restricted_pair_solver, ssi_admit::register_ssi_admit_solver) because they fall outside the A-C read scopes (fragment A is not yet filed at this dispatch). Every pub entry point in the read scope is accounted for: rule rows cover the proof-bearing dispatchers; pure data/accessor items are noted here as grouped or non-routing. bd_bridge.rs non-row pub items: LatheEdge/ProfileEdge/SolidSpec/RotationFrame/StationFrame/PartSpec/BooleanNode/TreeNode/Facts/Triangle are data carriers (SolidSpec and TreeNode serde dispatch are row D-BRIDGE-SOLIDSPEC-SERDE and the tree-node arms); prism_geom/prism_bbox/prism_mesh are grouped under D-BRIDGE-VOLUME-PRISM / D-BRIDGE-BBOX-LOCAL / D-BRIDGE-MESH-PRISM; write_tree_stl/bd_facts/bd_stl/tree_facts are rows. facade.rs non-row pub items: ModeValue/AxisValue/CarrierClass/SweptBooleanEvent/CertifiedBooleanRoute/SweptBooleanRefusal/BooleanPairVerdict/FacadeOp/FacadeTable/ExportEntry/FacadeReport/REPORT_SCHEMA are data carriers or outcomes consumed by the facade rows; CarrierClass::is_funnel_carrier is grouped under D-FACADE-BOOLEAN-DISPATCH and D-FACADE-BOOLEAN-PRODUCT. binding.rs non-row pub items: Bracket/MalformedRow/BindingError/ConeRow/BooleanRow/BooleanOutcome/VolumeRow/VolumeOutcome/TrimRow/TrimOutcome/TrimExtrudeRow/TrimCrossingRecord/TrimExtrudeOutcome/TrimExtrudeFacts/PatchRow are data carriers; ConeRow::to_cone is grouped under D-BINDING-BOOLEAN-DISPATCH; the eight binding #[pyfunction] wrappers are grouped under D-BINDING-PYO3-UNREGISTERED and their inner fns have rows. marshal.rs non-row pub items: ExceptionClass/RefusedPayload/Ledger/UnresolvedPayload/Marshaled/MarshaledPayload/DoorCase/UnmappedRefusal are data carriers; UnmappedRefusal::new/door_case/marshaled are grouped under D-MARSHAL-FROM-UNMAPPED; witness_name/prop_name/truth_name/collapse_reason_name/method_name/ledger_from_budget/door_case_of_construct_refusal are pure name/ledger accessors grouped under D-MARSHAL-FROM-REFUSAL and D-MARSHAL-KERNEL-KIND-NAME. door.py is a fixture harness: its _TRUCK_NAMES vocabulary, frame algebra helpers, profile reconstruction helpers and STL writer are grouped under their dispatch rows. No structural-mismatch STOP was triggered: every in-scope routing construct is expressible in the RULES schema; the unmodeled values are value/axis-level abstraction-gap findings (the axes have no carrier-class or op-name value), not shape failures. The nine routing gaps are the W_code vs W_theory delta: RG-1/RG-2/RG-3 are the certified boolean dispatch unreachable, RG-4 is the never-computed boolean product, RG-5/RG-6/RG-7 are the facade-table vs door-bridge divergence that refines the coarse OP_CAPABILITY_MATRIX cells, RG-8 is the occ/truck engine divergence, RG-9 is the test-only solid reflection. matrix_cells carries the coarse-cell -> semantic-route refinement relation for all 26 cells.
